verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes an implementation-relevant component-selection rule requiring a standard, readily sourceable USB connector.
The client adds compatible-alternative availability as a concrete acceptance condition for selecting the connector.
First concrete assembly-sourcing cost failure: numerous ordinary components incurred JLCPCB Extended-part setup fees.
Distinct sensor-board path: the selected connectors were concretely reported unavailable.
Distinct procurement failure: the selected connector acquired a 20-piece minimum order and materially higher unit cost.
The client revises the hardware-selection acceptance rule by permitting the high-MOQ connector when no suitable alternative exists; the superseded alternatives-only key is validly removed.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports replacing the missing components in the BOM.
Distinct main-board path after the replacement exchange: the two ESP32-adjacent connectors were found out of stock.
The client changes the BOM and assembly inclusion rule for optional main-board connectors based on availability and cost.
The client adds an implementation-relevant JLCPCB Basic-component preference for the integrated-board variant; administrative milestone and pricing content is not encoded.
